name: South Gate
amenities: Main entrance|Bus stop on Commons Avenue|Bike racks|Park office
summary: The main entrance on Commons Avenue, with the park office, the bus stop and the start of the Wallow Loop.
body:
The gates are opened by the park crew at 5:00 am and locked at 11:00 pm, every day of the year. The park office inside the gate is staffed 8:00 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays.

Most visitors arrive here: the Route 14 bus stops at the gate, and the Wallow is a five-minute walk north along the Elm Walk spur.

name: North Gate
amenities: Ridge Road parking (40 spaces)|Trailhead kiosk|Water fountain (Apr–Oct)
summary: The Ridge Road entrance and the trailhead for the Ridge Trail and Cadwallow Woods.
body: The North Gate lot fills by 9:00 am on fall weekends. The trailhead kiosk has a printed map and the day's trail conditions.

name: West Gate
summary: The Meadow Street entrance, where the city bike path joins the Perimeter Path.
body: A signalized crossing on Meadow Street leads straight onto the Meadow Path loop.

name: East Gate
summary: The Elm Walk entrance, closest to the Walled Garden and the boathouse.
body: The East Gate has the park's accessible parking and the flattest route to the water, along the Elm Walk.

name: The Wallow Boathouse
amenities: Rowboat and paddleboat rentals|Life jackets for every size|Snack window|Restrooms (seasonal)
summary: The 1928 boathouse on the north shore of the Wallow. Boats from May to September.
body:
The boathouse was built in 1928 by the city's Works Department and restored in 2019. Rowboats and paddleboats are rented on a walk-up basis; there is nothing to book in advance.

Out of season the building is closed, but the terrace and the shoreline benches stay open.

name: Hillcrest Overlook
amenities: Stone bench ring|View across the Wallow to downtown
summary: The highest point in the park, 742 feet, at the top of the Ridge Trail.
body:
The ring of stone benches was laid in 1936. On a clear evening you can see across the Wallow to the downtown skyline, three miles south.

The woods trails close at dusk: there is no lighting under the trees.

name: Tanner's Run Boardwalk
amenities: Boardwalk over the wetland|Two bird blinds|Interpretive signs
summary: A boardwalk over the wetland where Tanner's Run slows before it reaches the Wallow.
body: The boardwalk is being replaced in sections this fall; see park projects. Section 3, nearest the Wallow, is closed until the new decking is in.

name: Long Meadow
summary: Forty-one acres of open meadow on the west side, mown in paths and left long at the edges.
body: The middle of the meadow is mown for picnics, kites and frisbee. The edges are being converted to native prairie in plots tended by the Friends of Cadwallow Park.

name: Commons Playground
summary: The main playground on the South Commons. To be rebuilt as an all-abilities playground in 2027.
body: The current playground dates from 2004. The rebuild is in the bidding phase; the old playground stays open until construction starts.

name: Splash Pad
amenities: Ground jets and water arch|Changing room
summary: Ground jets and a water arch next to the playground. Runs June through August.
body: The water is recirculated and treated, and the pad is checked every morning by the crew before it opens.

name: Ballfields 1–3
amenities: Three lit diamonds|Dugouts and bleachers|Batting cage
summary: Three lit diamonds on the South Commons, used by city leagues most evenings.
body: League schedules take priority. Open play is first come, first served when a field is not booked.

name: Linden Shelter
amenities: Twelve picnic tables|Four grills|Electric outlets|Restrooms nearby
summary: The largest picnic shelter, under a stand of old lindens at the edge of the Long Meadow.
body: Reservations are made by phone with the Parks and Recreation office. When it is not reserved, the shelter is first come, first served.

name: Elm Walk Shelter
amenities: Six picnic tables|Two grills|View of the Wallow
summary: A smaller shelter on the Elm Walk with a view down to the Wallow.
body: Popular for birthday parties. Reserve by phone; unreserved days are first come, first served.

name: The Walled Garden
amenities: Formal beds and glasshouse|Ginkgo pair|Volunteer-run plant sale (May)
summary: A one-acre walled garden from 1911, with a small glasshouse, formal beds and the oldest ginkgos in the city.
body: The garden is locked outside its hours to protect the glasshouse. In winter the glasshouse is the warmest place in the park.

name: South Restrooms
summary: Heated restrooms next to the playground, open all year.
body: Cleaned twice a day by the park crew.

name: Meadow Restrooms
summary: Seasonal restrooms on the Long Meadow. Winterized from November to March.
body: In winter use the South Restrooms, a twelve-minute walk along the Perimeter Path.

name: Warming Hut
amenities: Wood stove|Skate benches|Hot drinks on weekends
summary: A timber hut on the south shore of the Wallow, open in winter for skaters and walkers.
body: The hut opens in December whether or not the Wallow freezes. Skating is allowed only when the crew post the ice as open on the conditions board.
